course_name_original: Laboratory of technologies and sustainability of polymers
course_name_en: Laboratory of technologies and sustainability of polymers
prerequisites: Good basic knowledge of General Chemistry

learning_outcomes.text: Acquisition of knowledge relating to the main technologies used in plastics processing, with particular regard to aspects linked to the environmental sustainability of raw materials, transformation processes and end-of-life management.
Understanding the main technologies used in plastics transformation, and the correlations between the process parameters used and the resulting technological properties.
Learn about the processing machines needed for plastics transformation, with relative process parameter settings.
Acquire the basic tools for assessing the environmental impact of different types of plastics, related transformation technologies and end-of-life processes.
Propose the most suitable production process for a plastic product, also in relation to the environmental balance of the process and end-of-life management.
Carry out group laboratory activities related to process technologies and characterisation of plastics, with particular attention to innovative and sustainable materials and processes.
Present the experimental results in a comprehensive manner through an oral presentation and technical report.

syllabus_topics: Polymeric materials: definition, classification, environmental impact, presentation of the main types of plastics
Thermoplastic materials transformation processes: melt compounding, extrusion, thermoforming, moulding
Thermosetting materials transformation processes: compression moulding, manual lamination, resin transfer moulding, resin infusion
Elastomers transformation processes: compounding, incorporation of additives, vulcanisation
End-of-life management of plastics: landfill, waste-to-energy, recycling, biodegradation/composting
Physical characterisation of the manufactured products (thermo-mechanical properties)
teaching_methods: Preparation and presentation of individual PowerPoint reports

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam on the theoretical content of the course (individual)

assessment_rules: The final exam consists of three mandatory parts: group reports (max 8 points), an oral presentation (max 7 points), and an oral exam (max 15 points). The exam can only be considered sufficient if the oral exam assessment is greater than or equal to 9/15. Group reports must be submitted at least 5 days before the exam and within 60 days of the end of the course. The presentation must be submitted in PDF format the day before the exam. Cum Laude may be attributed at the discretion of the teacher.
